_comment: Field-reading probe on the best arm: a tool-less haiku reads one bare response (interpretation and derived stripped) and states per field its meaning, unit, kind and null meaning; scored against evals/field-probe/best-*-truth.json.
model: haiku (claude -p, --tools '', empty MCP config, empty cwd)
calibration: BEFORE the scored runs, after one smoke run: the truth file was widened (floor areas may be 'measured', status fields 'metadata', VBO count/coordinates tool-derived) — recorded in the truth file's _calibration.

AFTER the scored runs, rescored from the saved answers with no new model calls: 'calculated' accepted where the truth allows 'computed_by_tool' (both mean derived, not observed), and 'degree-days' accepted as a spelling of °C·day. Raw and rescored summaries are both below.
headline: building: 41 of 44 fields pass kind + unit 9/9, the other 3 8/9. Every calculated-only energy field read as CALCULATED, never MEASURED (0 of 99 readings). sbi_sector_omschrijving read as a description 9/9 after the rename. All 14 UNCOVERED_BY_DESIGN fields pass: their names need no explanation. BUT reading the meanings (not the auto-score) shows one real scope misread: oppervlakte_bag_verblijfsobject_m2 read as the BUILDING's area in 2 of 9 ('Total floor area of building') — the Dutch 'verblijfsobject' in the name does not carry 'one unit' for haiku. The response rule bp.area.one_unit covers it; the name alone does not.

weather: meanings right in every reading; the critical distinctions right 3/3 (weightedHdd vs hdd, archive vs forecast, reference vs actual). 7 fields stay flagged after rescoring, all on unit spelling ('days' for a count) or kind choice (label = metadata, the 2800 constant = register). One real meaning error: cdd with base 26 °C (1 of 3; the base is 18).
Lesson for the instrument, as for eval rubrics (H2): an automatic kind/unit score is a filter; the flagged rows must be read.
